questions.stem: In the context of the Indian Constitution, the 'Right to Property', which was originally a Fundamental Right, is now a:
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Originally, the Right to Property was a Fundamental Right under Article 31. However, it caused massive legal hurdles for the government trying to implement land reforms and abolish the Zamindari system. The 44th Amendment Act (1978) deleted it from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a simple 'Legal Right' under a new Article 300A in Part XII.
DECOY BUSTING: It is not a Directive Principle. If it were a fundamental right, you could go directly to the Supreme Court if the government acquired your land for a highway without your consent. As a legal right, you can only go to the High Court for regular compensation.
EXAM INSIGHT: This is one of the most frequently asked questions in Indian Polity. Always associate it with the 44th Amendment.
